## Coloring Arguments (Necessary Conditions)

**Coloring 1: $c(i,j) = (i+j) \bmod 3$.**

Every horizontal tromino covering $(i,j),(i,j{+}1),(i,j{+}2)$ hits colors $(i{+}j), (i{+}j{+}1), (i{+}j{+}2) \pmod{3}$ — one of each. Every vertical tromino covering $(i,j),(i{+}1,j),(i{+}2,j)$ hits colors $(i{+}j),(i{+}j{+}1),(i{+}j{+}2) \pmod{3}$ — one of each. So each of the 21 plates covers exactly one cell of each color, covering 21 cells per color.

Counting cells of each color on the $8\times 8$ board (using the distribution of $i{+}j$ values):

| Color | $i{+}j$ values | Count |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| 0 | 3,6,9,12,15 | $2{+}5{+}8{+}5{+}2 = 22$ |
| 1 | 4,7,10,13,16 | $3{+}6{+}7{+}4{+}1 = 21$ |
| 2 | 2,5,8,11,14 | $1{+}4{+}7{+}6{+}3 = 21$ |

Since 21 plates cover 21 of each color, the uncovered cell must be the **excess** cell of color 0: $(i{+}j)\equiv 0\pmod{3}$.

**Coloring 2: $c(i,j) = (i-j)\bmod 3$.**

By the same reasoning (consecutive values mod 3 in both orientations), each plate covers one of each color. Counting:

| Color | Count |
|-------|-------|
| 0 ($i\equiv j$) | $4{+}9{+}9 = 22$ |
| 1 ($i\equiv j{+}1$) | $6{+}9{+}6 = 21$ |
| 2 ($i\equiv j{+}2$) | $6{+}6{+}9 = 21$ |

The uncovered cell must satisfy $(i{-}j)\equiv 0\pmod{3}$, i.e., $i\equiv j\pmod{3}$.

**Combining:** $(i{+}j)\equiv 0$ and $(i{-}j)\equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ gives $2i\equiv 0$ and $2j\equiv 0\pmod{3}$, hence $i\equiv 0$ and $j\equiv 0\pmod{3}$ (since $\gcd(2,3)=1$).

With $1\le i,j\le 8$: $i\in\{3,6\}$, $j\in\{3,6\}$, yielding exactly **4 candidates**: $(3,3),(3,6),(6,3),(6,6)$.

**No further constraints:** The checkerboard coloring $(i{+}j)\bmod 2$ yields no restriction (both parities are consistent). The two mod-3 colorings above are the only independent linear colorings valid for both tromino orientations.

## Sufficiency: Explicit Tiling with $(3,3)$ Uncovered

I construct a valid tiling of the $8\times 8$ board minus cell $(3,3)$:

| # | Tromino | Type |

| 13 | $(5,6)(5,7)(5,8)$ | horizontal |
| 14–21 | $(6,j)(7,j)(8,j)$ for $j=1,\dots,8$ | vertical |

**Verification:** Every cell in rows 1–8 is covered exactly once, except $(3,3)$ which is the hole. The 21 trominoes cover $63$ cells. ✓

## All Four Candidates Are Achievable

The board's symmetries (reflections/rotations preserving the tromino set) map $(3,3)$ to the other candidates:
- Vertical reflection $(i,j)\to(i,9{-}j)$: $(3,3)\to(3,6)$
- Horizontal reflection $(i,j)\to(9{-}i,j)$: $(3,3)\to(6,3)$
- $180°$ rotation $(i,j)\to(9{-}i,9{-}j)$: $(3,3)\to(6,6)$

Since $(3,3)$ is achievable and these symmetries preserve the tiling problem, all four cells are achievable.

## Final Computation

The valid uncovered cells are $(3,3),\,(3,6),\,(6,3),\,(6,6)$.

$$\text{Sum} = (3{+}3)+(3{+}6)+(6{+}3)+(6{+}6) = 6+9+9+12 = \boxed{36}$$
